topic: Luffy gave Ace's Mera Mera no Mi to Sabo because the one fruit per body rule made it the only way to keep the flame in the family
title: Why Luffy Couldn't Eat Ace's Fruit (Sabo Got It)
description: Luffy won the Mera Mera no Mi in Dressrosa, then handed it to Sabo. Here's the Devil Fruit rule that explains why, and the one exception it breaks. Should Luffy have kept it, or did Sabo deserve it?
comment: Did Sabo deserve Ace's fruit more than Luffy, or should Luffy have given it to someone else? Pick one.

lines.text: Luffy couldn't eat Ace's fruit. That's the real reason Sabo got it.

shot.search: Sabo Mera Mera no Mi Luffy
shot.fallback: flame wielding blond man facing a rubber boy

lines.text: I think most fans treat this as a sweet moment. It's actually a rule.

shot.fallback: two brothers crying in an arena

lines.text: In Dressrosa, Luffy fights through a whole colosseum to win the Mera Mera fruit.

shot.fallback: rubber hero fighting in a colosseum

lines.text: Then Sabo steps in, shoves Bartolomeo aside, and calls Luffy by name.
And Luffy lets him eat it.
People say Luffy was just being kind. But look at his own body.
He already ate the Gum-Gum Fruit as a kid, and one body can only hold one fruit.
Eat a second one and you die. Blackbeard is the only exception we've seen.
So the fruit had to go to someone, or Ace's fire would vanish.

shot.search: Ace Mera Mera no Mi fire fist
shot.fallback: fire fist swordless fighter in flames

lines.text: And Sabo already lost his memory once, then got it back when Ace died.
So the flame didn't pass to a stranger. It stayed in the brothers.
Luffy couldn't eat Ace's fruit, so Sabo got it.
